items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1983-05-28
items.q: I certainly know that Edmont gave one of the library branches in town a quite extensive collection of records.

ctx.x: Let's see. We talked about the Sushant some before and their role. I think one thing that we can't realize is how many jobs the Jazz Club got for people. The society functions. I think there's a lot of work like that going on. And we only heard about it.
I think that's totally true. I certainly know that Edmont gave one of the library branches in town a quite extensive collection of records. I think some very early. Mm-hmm. I was impressed by that.
Yeah. And they found work for their particular favorites. Sure. Yeah. Let's see. We talked about the Southern Yacht Club before.

items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-07-31
items.q: through people like Myra Menville and Dr. Edmond Suchant

ctx.x: Yeah. In any case, bands then were very willing to audition and to try out. And there was a certain amount of work with private parties going on through people like Myra Menville and Dr. Edmond Suchant. Yeah. And that may have, they may have invited you out there. It would just be the only way I could think of.

I don't, no, I don't think it was one of them. I expect it might come to me, but I don't remember. I know what would happen, you know, would be somebody would, sometimes you, sometimes Bob Greenwood, sometimes, I think I went to several places with Joan Whitehead when she was in New Orleans. Various people would get in touch and say, you know, what's his name is playing out at such and such a place, let's go. And sometimes I'd say, we'll be able to get in, and they'd say, oh sure, the musicians will say it's…

items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-01
items.q: I suspect Aksushan probably was one of them, despite some of our annoyances with him.

ctx.x: Let's see, we talked about the Grand Marshals, and you talked about the Eureka recording session. Yeah, I have a feeling about that. Uh, did you, we were talking about social classes, and you know, really nice people didn't do this, and so forth. And so forth, and... I guess there were some nice people who even listened to jazz, but it had to be the right band. I think, too. I think that was fun.

Well, I suspect that there were some nice people who thought for themselves and did not... Mm-hmm. ...didn't feel as encumbered as other people did. I suspect Aksushan probably was one of them, despite some of our annoyances with him.

items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-02
items.q: which Edmond Suchon had given to the library

ctx.x: And, uh, I think we were all very different back then. And had some different ideas and a lot of, a lot of discomforts and fears which hang on in some ways now despite the fact that there's no need for it.

Yeah, well, she was offended that she couldn't come to the New Orleans Public Library to hear her old records, which Edmond Suchon had given to the library. I can't remember when that was exactly that I was working on cataloging them. stuff

I'd have to look that up, but she, yeah, that's one of the things. That was in the mid-50s. Yeah, that angered her. Yeah, it would have been mid-50s maybe, maybe 53, 54, something like that.
